name: Renu Energy Solutions
old_description: Renu Energy Solutions is a locally owned solar installer serving North and South Carolina since 2010. With regional offices across the Southeast, Renu provides high-quality solar energy system installations for homes and businesses, along with energy storage, EV charging, and system monitoring.
about:
Renu Energy Solutions was founded in 2010 in Charlotte, North Carolina, as a locally owned solar installation company serving North and South Carolina. The firm operates regional offices across the Southeast.

The company provides turn-key solar energy system installations for residential and commercial customers, including energy storage, EV charging, and system monitoring. All installations are performed by in-house W2 employees rather than subcontractors. Renu holds both general contractor and electrical contractor licenses, and its staff includes NABCEP-certified professionals. To date, the company has completed over 6,000 solar installations and more than 1,500 energy storage installations across the Southeast.

Renu serves homeowners, businesses, nonprofits, and municipalities throughout the Carolinas and the broader Southeast. Commercial clients range from small businesses to corporations, and the company manages utility interconnection processes such as Duke Energy's PowerPair program. Residential projects include custom-designed solar arrays, battery backup systems from brands like Tesla Powerwall, FranklinWH, and Generac, and whole-home standby generators.

Renu differentiates itself through a fully integrated, in-house model that handles design, permitting, utility applications, and installation under one roof. The company cites its policy of adjusting customer contracts when material costs decrease as an example of its commitment to transparency. Licensing, certification, and direct employment of installers are presented as the foundation of consistent quality and accountability.

name: Republic Wire Inc
old_description: Since its humble beginnings in a 3000 sq ft warehouse in 1982, Republic Wire has grown to over 400,000 sq ft and continues to grow. Republic Wire was founded on the principals of service for our customers. Hard work, customer loyalty and the ability to manufacture a quality product are Republic Wire’s key ingredients for success.
about:
Republic Wire Inc. began operations in Cincinnati, Ohio, in January 1982. Founder Ron Rosenbeck, who had been in the copper industry since 1973, started the company in a 3,000-square-foot warehouse. The business remains under his ownership as CEO.

The company manufactures a range of copper and aluminum wiring products, including bare copper, THHN, XHHW, USE, NM-B, TFFN, TW, polyweatherproof, tinned copper, PV, UF, MHF, URD, SER, SEU, and aluminum variants. Production uses electrolytically refined 99% pure copper insulated with polyvinyl chloride, with in-line testing for imperfections. The operation now occupies a 350,000-square-foot modern production facility in West Chester Township, Ohio.

Republic Wire serves electrical wholesale distributors, utility distributors, Rural Utilities Service (RUS) cooperatives, investor-owned utilities, and municipalities nationwide. Its product line is designed to meet the needs of these customer segments with an emphasis on inventory availability and fill rates.

The company was founded on principles of customer service, hard work, and loyalty, with a commitment to delivering high-quality products on time. Republic Wire emphasizes its USA manufacturing and a team-based approach to quality and service.

name: RevoluSun Solar
old_description: Locally owned and operated since 2009. We specialize in residential and commercial solar panel installation, Tesla Powerwall battery storage, Tesla Solar Roof, and EV charging.
about:
RevoluSun Solar is a locally owned and operated solar installation company headquartered in Boise, Idaho. The business traces its roots to a flagship location opened in Hawaii in 2009, before expanding to the Pacific Northwest with a Boise office in 2019 and a Coeur d’Alene office in 2022. The company serves all of Idaho, Washington, and Oregon from its Mountain States division.

The firm provides full-service solar and energy storage installation for residential and commercial customers. Its offerings include rooftop and ground-mounted solar panel systems, Tesla Solar Roof installations, battery storage using Tesla Powerwall, Sonnen, FranklinWH, and Enphase products, and EV charger installation with Tesla Wall Connector and SPAN Drive equipment. RevoluSun manages the entire process from energy assessment and system design through permitting, inspection, and utility interconnection. To date, the company has completed over 10,000 installations across the Pacific Northwest.

RevoluSun works with homeowners, businesses, and property owners seeking grid resilience and energy independence. Its residential clients include households adding solar, backup batteries, and EV charging, while commercial projects range from small businesses to larger facilities. The company’s project portfolio spans Idaho, eastern Washington, and Oregon, with installations tailored to the region’s climate and utility requirements.

The company emphasizes its Tesla Certified Energy Installer status and a design approach built for the Pacific Northwest’s specific weather and energy patterns. Its stated mission is “building the future of energy by taking care of people and always doing the right thing,” focusing on local expertise, durable products, and seamless project management.

name: Revolution Performance Fabrics
old_description: Founded in 2014, Revolution is part of STI Fabrics — a North Carolina mill weaving performance fabric since 1964. Our
about:
Revolution Performance Fabrics operates from Kings Mountain, North Carolina, where it has woven performance upholstery fabrics since launching in 2014 as a brand under STI Fabrics — a mill that has been producing textiles in the region since 1964. The company is part of a family-owned textile heritage, though the current ownership structure is not publicly detailed.

The mill designs and weaves its fabrics using Olefin yarn and upcycled fibers, producing stain-resistant, bleach-cleanable materials that are free of PFAS, formaldehyde, heavy metals, phenols, phthalates, and flame retardants. The product range includes jacquards, solids, chenilles, and machine-washable options for both indoor and outdoor applications, all manufactured at the Kings Mountain facility. Specific production volumes, headcount, and equipment details are not disclosed.

The fabrics serve residential furniture makers, outdoor furniture manufacturers, interior designers, and drapery workrooms. Revolution’s trade program caters to members of ASID, IDS, and VRD, offering preferred pricing and dedicated support. Customer reviews highlight use cases such as reupholstering patio furniture and specifying fabrics for client projects, with the Heritage Collection — tailored stripes, plush chenille, and textured wovens — cited as a recent addition.

The brand was created to demonstrate that high-performance upholstery does not require “forever chemicals.” By eliminating PFAS and other hazardous substances while maintaining durability and cleanability, Revolution positions its PFAS-free construction as a safer choice for homes with children and pets.

about:
Rex Plastics operates from Vancouver, Washington, where it has been manufacturing plastic injection molded parts since 1971. The company is a second-generation, family-owned and operated contract manufacturer that began with a focus on domestic mold building and material sourcing.

The shop provides full-service injection molding, including mold design and construction backed by a lifetime guarantee, design-for-manufacturing assistance, prototyping via 3D printing, first-article inspection, and production runs from short-run to high-volume. Secondary operations encompass pad printing, hydrographics, assembly, packaging, and light distribution. The facility produces components such as the 200,000 squeegees it molds annually for Artscape.

Rex Plastics serves OEMs and startups across sports equipment, electronics, medical, communications, and consumer products. Its client roster includes International Electronics, Boyd Coffee, Artscape, Stormwater Management, Pacific Coast Marine, and Trident Design, among others. The company reports a 98 percent OEM retention rate over the past decade.

The firm differentiates itself by insisting on U.S.-built molds and domestically sourced raw materials whenever possible, offering a lifetime mold guarantee, and providing end-to-end service from concept through retail-ready packaging. Founders emphasize a commitment to positive community impact and long-term customer relationships.

about:
Ricardo Food Group Inc. operates from New York City and was founded in 1991 by Ricardo Cordero. The firm began as a consulting practice focused on helping food brands navigate contract manufacturing relationships.

The company functions as an advisory firm specializing in sourcing co-packing, private label, and contract manufacturing partnerships for the food, bakery, beverage, and plant-based sectors. It maintains an active portfolio of more than 600 U.S.-based manufacturing facilities and leverages 35 years of production expertise to match clients with suitable partners. Beyond sourcing, RFG provides advisory services for acquisitions, debt restructuring, management buyouts, and capital investment strategies.

Clients range from emerging brands seeking to expand capacity to established companies pursuing economies of scale. The firm serves the food, bakery, beverage, and plant-based industries, assisting with product line extensions, brand rejuvenation, and cost control.

RFG emphasizes its deep relationships with contract manufacturers as a core differentiator, stating that its network often yields cost-saving or value-added benefits clients might not identify independently. The firm positions itself as a bridge between brands and production resources, aiming to reduce the risk and complexity of sourcing manufacturing partners.

The company supplies all-wood cabinets with no particle board, along with granite countertops, through a showroom that carries an in-stock Shaker White line deliverable in 14 days and a quick-ship program offering 36 colors in three to five weeks. It sources products from wholesalers that typically deliver within five to six business days, and provides personalized design services seven days a week.

about:
Richard Bissell Fine Woodworking, Inc. operates a small woodworking shop in Putney, Vermont. Founded in 1982 by Richard Bissell, the business began as a one-person operation designing and building handmade furniture piece by piece. Over four decades it has grown into a direct-to-consumer maker of Shaker, Mission, and Windsor-style furniture, with a showroom on site.

The shop produces beds, tables, case pieces, seating, desks, and custom built-ins using solid hardwoods and traditional joinery. Each piece is handmade in the Vermont workshop, with construction details covering bed, chair, table, and drawer assembly. The company also offers customization of standard models and fully custom designs, finishing with hand-applied wood finishes.

Furniture is sold directly to residential customers through the website and the Putney showroom, eliminating gallery or retailer markups. The client base consists of individual homeowners seeking heirloom-quality pieces; no wholesale or contract manufacturing is mentioned.

Bissell emphasizes thoughtful design, sustainable lumber sourcing, and a lifetime guarantee on all work. The direct-sales model keeps pricing fair, while the workshop’s focus on proportion, clean details, and durable joinery aims to deliver functional beauty at a reasonable value.

about:
Richard Plastics Co. has operated from Laurel, Mississippi since 1948, when it was founded to supply custom injection-molded thermoplastic parts at affordable prices. The company remains privately held, though ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The 22,700-square-foot facility houses computer-controlled Milacron molding machines that run small to medium production runs, from a few hundred parts up to hundreds of thousands. In-house capabilities include custom injection molding of thermoplastics, on-site mold building and repair through a comprehensive toolroom, and secondary operations such as assembly, hot stamping, heat transfer, machining, and pad printing.

The molder serves customers in furniture, water-valve, and precision military-component sectors, working from design sketches through finished parts. Its toolroom can refine existing mold designs or develop new ones to improve cost efficiency.

The company emphasizes on-time delivery, competitive pricing, and a quality system aimed at defect-free parts, citing decades-long customer relationships as evidence of its reliability.

about:
Richards Sheet Metal was founded in 1928 in Ogden, Utah. The company has operated continuously for nearly a century, though the original founders are not named in available sources.

The company operates a 90,000-square-foot facility where it provides a range of metal fabrication services. These include flat sheet laser cutting, tube laser cutting, CNC/turret punching, precision sheet metal forming, welding (with certified welders and orbital welding capability), architectural and decorative sheet metal fabrication, field services, painting and coating systems, tool design, prototyping, and stamping. Richards handles both one-off parts and mass-produced components.

Its customer base spans transportation, waste management, military and government, mining, food services and sanitation, machinery, construction and architectural, institutional and recreational, pharmaceuticals, general industrial, farming, and entrepreneurial start-ups.

Richards positions itself as a total solution for quality metal fabrication, emphasizing its state-of-the-art facility and ability to deliver innovative solutions that exceed performance and quality expectations.

about:
Righteous began in the late 1980s when Aly and Rick Salz, frustrated by inconsistent quality and unreliable vendors in the corporate apparel market, launched Righteous Clothing Agency in Pasadena, California. The company later moved its headquarters to Clackamas, Oregon, where it operates today.

Today Righteous operates as a full-service apparel partner, handling custom screen printing, embroidery, design, warehousing, kitting, and fulfillment through a dual-warehouse network in Oregon and Missouri. The company manages online company stores for clients ranging from small teams to enterprises with thousands of employees, processing orders with real-time inventory and shipping in-stock items within two days. A staff of around 1,000 supports end-to-end program management, from creative design to nationwide distribution.

Righteous serves clients across restaurants and food service, industrial manufacturing and construction, healthcare, education, and grocery and convenience sectors. Its customer base includes multi-location restaurant chains such as Farrelli’s Pizza and Elmer’s Restaurants, construction firms like Pence Contractors, healthcare networks such as PeaceHealth, and brands including Dave & Buster’s, Great Harvest, and Craveworthy Brands.

The company was founded to solve the problem of messy printing, crooked logos, and vendors who disappointed when it mattered most. Righteous differentiates itself by assigning a dedicated account manager to each client, providing real-time inventory visibility, and managing the entire workflow from design through fulfillment so clients don’t have to juggle multiple vendors.

name: Rimer & Rimer Plastic Division
old_description: We offer injection molding services throughout the southeast US. We process most commercially available thermoplastics.
about:
Rimer & Rimer Plastic Division operates from Bradenton, Florida, where it was founded in 1989. The company has remained family-owned for over three decades, building a reputation as a dependable supplier of custom injection molding services across the southeastern United States.

The facility spans 25,000 square feet of dedicated manufacturing space and houses 14 injection molding machines ranging from 75 to 770 U.S. tons, with shot capacities from 3 to 128 ounces. Core processes include injection molding, insert molding, over molding, blade and insert molding, magnetic additive molding, custom color and effects molding, and molding of X-ray detectable, metal detectable, and thermally conductive plastics. The company also provides tooling and part design, R&D tooling and sampling, assembly from basic to complex, and packaging design.

Rimer & Rimer serves a broad customer base in consumer goods — lawn and garden, pool equipment, kitchenware, sporting goods, and musical accessories — as well as construction and agriculture markets with window and door components, HVAC parts, and heavy equipment assemblies. Rescue and safety equipment manufacturers rely on the shop for strobe light components, over-molded knives and sheaths, buckles, harnesses, housings, guards, and shields. The company emphasizes its specialization in hard-to-mold materials.

The firm distinguishes itself by offering a wider range of part sizes than most molders in the state, often acting as a single source for all injection molding needs. Its stated focus on difficult materials, combined with in-house assembly and packaging, aims to reduce supply-chain complexity for customers.

about:
Roanoke Electronic Controls (REC) operates from Roanoke, Alabama, where it has delivered custom electronic solutions for over 25 years. The company was established as a U.S.-based manufacturer dedicated to the design and production of quality electronic controls, offering a turn-key service that takes a concept through design, prototyping, and production.

REC provides full-spectrum engineering and manufacturing under one roof. Its in-house capabilities span schematic design, PCB layout, firmware and embedded software development, and mobile app creation for connected products. On the production side, the facility runs automated SMT assembly with two pick-and-place machines, leaded and lead-free wave soldering, selective soldering, through-hole insertion, automated conformal coating (acrylic, silicone, urethane, epoxy), AOI inspection, and a dedicated BGA/QFP rework station. Every board receives 100% electrical testing. The shop supports prototype runs of 5–25 units through production volumes of 10,000+ units, with a sweet spot in the 500–1,000 unit range.

The company serves a range of industries including outdoor cooking (controllers for brands such as Blaz’n Grill Works and Pitts & Spitts), sports timing (electronics for Victory Game Clocks’ wireless scoreboards and play clocks), alternative energy, industrial monitoring, and fitness equipment. Its Navy-certified soldering expertise also makes it a candidate for military and defense-adjacent programs. Customers include startups and OEMs that need direct engineering access throughout the product lifecycle.

REC emphasizes several differentiators: all engineering is performed in-house by the same team that oversees manufacturing, eliminating handoffs; the quality system is registered to ANSI/ISO 9001:2015 with full traceability; manufacturing is 100% U.S.-based, avoiding overseas delays; and customers work directly with engineers rather than sales intermediaries. The firm also highlights its military-grade soldering capability and true turn-key partnership from napkin sketch to production run.

about:
Roehm America LLC, headquartered in Osceola, Arkansas, operates as the Americas division of Röhm GmbH, a global manufacturer of methacrylate monomers and polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) products. The company supplies the Americas under the ACRYLITE® and ACRYMID® trademarks, while its European, Asian, African and Australian markets are served under the PLEXIGLAS® and PLEXIMID® brands.

The company produces a complete range of PMMA-based standard, impact-modified and special molding compounds. Its Bay City, Texas facility runs the world’s first full-scale industrial operation of the proprietary LiMA technology for methyl methacrylate (MMA) production. Processes include injection compression molding and mold-in-color compounding, which eliminates a separate coating step. The global workforce numbers approximately 2,700 employees.

Roehm serves the automotive, electronics, construction and medical technology industries. In automotive, Volkswagen and its supplier Magna use colored PLEXIGLAS® molding compounds for mold-in-color rear spoilers on the ID. Buzz. Construction and outdoor markets use ACRYLITE® SunResist capstock for window profiles, decking, furniture and façades. The company also supplies medical-grade methacrylate materials.

Roehm emphasizes decarbonization through its methacrylate Verbund. The LiMA process reduces the carbon footprint of MMA production. PLEXIGLAS® proTerra grades incorporate mechanically recycled PMMA or sustainably certified raw materials. Mold-in-color manufacturing cuts emissions by avoiding energy-intensive coating. The ACRYLITE® SunResist capstock extends product life in high-exposure outdoor applications.

name: Royal Plastics Inc
old_description: With 40 years of experience in molding and tooling, we can find an answer to almost any molding problem.
about:
Royal Plastics, Inc. operates from a 46,000-square-foot facility in Brookings, South Dakota. The company was started in 1978 by Arlen and Jane Rosvold and remains family-owned; today it is held by their children, Michael Peterson and Renee Novak, with the next generation represented by Thomas Peterson as assistant vice president and production manager. The business moved into its current plant in March 1999.

As a custom injection molder of thermoplastics, Royal Plastics runs 15 molding machines ranging from 50 to 300 tons, six of which are all-electric. The shop produces parts from small gram weights up to two pounds, maintaining over 1,300 active part numbers for more than 200 customers across the United States and Canada. A full-service tool room handles mold maintenance, new mold construction, and engineering changes, while an in-house engineering team uses AutoCAD and SolidWorks for mold and part design. Prototyping is supported by a Fortus 250mc 3D printer (10×10×12 in. build envelope, ABSplus-P430 material, ±0.0095 in. accuracy). Quality control relies on a Keyence IM-6120 image dimension system (±2 µm accuracy) and a Mitutoyo QM-Height 600 gauge, backed by a dedicated maintenance program.

The company serves the window and door industry—where it has 40 years of experience—and the after-market automotive sector, among other markets. Its customer base spans OEMs and tier suppliers in both the U.S. and Canada.

Royal Plastics emphasizes a problem-solving culture (“we like problems”) and cites four guiding principles: putting the customer first, imposing no resin restrictions, maintaining dependable quality, and reducing costs. These differentiators are reinforced by on-site mold storage, stocking programs, and design assistance from concept through production.

Rudolph Foods Co is headquartered in Lima, Ohio, a city known as the "Pork Rind Capital of the World." The business remains family-owned, with the Rudolph family's original recipe—credited to Mary Rudolph—still at the core of its product line. The Lima campus houses corporate offices, a main pellet production facility, and a packaging plant. The company extended its footprint to the Southeast in 1994 with a 38,000-square-foot facility in Lawrenceville, Georgia, and to the Southwest in 2003 with a packaging operation in Dallas, Texas capable of 15 million pounds annually. Rudolph Foods acquired Whitefeather Foods, a Wapakoneta, Ohio pork rind maker founded in 1984, in 2000, and later added Lee's Pig Skins in New Hebron, Mississippi.

The company manufactures pork rinds and cracklins through pellet production and packaging processes. Its Lawrenceville plant produces up to 10 million pounds per year, while the Dallas facility handles up to 15 million pounds. Additional production sites in Wapakoneta, New Hebron, and Beaumont, California, along with international locations in Brazil, Mexico, and Denmark, support a multi-plant network. The firm also offers pellet production and packaging services to customers under its "Packaging / Pellet Customer Service" capability.

Rudolph Foods serves the snack food industry, supplying pork rind products to retail and foodservice channels. The company highlights its family recipe and consistent quality as key differentiators. In 2010, the Lawrenceville facility earned the U.S. Department of Energy's Energy Saver recognition for achieving more than 75,000 MMBtu in total energy savings.

name: SEMPAC
old_description: DEVELOPMENT & MANUFACTURING OF OPEN CAVITY PACKAGES FOR SEMICONDUCTORS
about:
SEMPAC is a privately-owned semiconductor packaging company based in Beaverton, Oregon, in the region known as the Silicon Forest. Founded in 2000 by veterans of the integrated circuit assembly industry, the company was created to offer a more reliable and less expensive alternative to the JEDEC-compliant packages then used for device prototyping and testing. The founders leveraged 50 years of combined experience to develop packaging solutions that did not require specialized assembly equipment or complicated storage.

The company designs, develops, and manufactures pre-molded open cavity plastic packages under the Open-Pak™ brand. Its product line spans QFN, QFP, SOIC, and SSOP architectures in body sizes from 3×3 mm to 12×12 mm, lead counts from 8 to 100, and lead pitches of 0.4 mm to 1.0 mm. Packages are molded with green (halogen-free) compounds, plated with gold over nickel for bondability, and conform to JEDEC outlines. SEMPAC also produces B-Stage lids and offers custom package design. All materials are RoHS 3 and REACH compliant.

SEMPAC serves the semiconductor assembly sector, supplying packages for high-frequency RF, optoelectronics, and power devices in both military and commercial applications. Its customers include integrated circuit manufacturers and assembly houses that need prototyping and test packages without the constraints of traditional contract manufacturing. The company emphasizes collaborative partnerships and does not compete with its customers.

SEMPAC differentiates itself through independence—remaining free of conflicts of interest—and a quality culture that includes inspection at every production stage, from raw material validation to final shipment. The company also commits to environmental responsibility, ensuring products are free of heavy metals per RoHS 3 (EU Directive 2015/863), and to ethical labor practices throughout its supply chain.

about:
SK Food Group traces its roots to 1942 when it began as a mobile catering operation in Seattle, Washington. The company, now headquartered in Reno, Nevada, has grown through a series of ownership changes and name transitions—including Don Campbell's Quality Food Service in 1979 and Stover's Kitchen in 2004—before selling its catering division in 2006 to focus exclusively on food manufacturing.

Today the company operates nine state-of-the-art facilities across the United States and Canada, employing more than 2,000 associates. Its plants are custom-built for Ready-to-Eat production, featuring motorized conveyor systems, precision slicing lines for meat and cheese, and extensive cold-storage, dry-storage, and dock infrastructure. All locations are USDA or CFIA certified and carry SQF Version 9.1 certification; the Burnsville and Lakeville, Minnesota sites also hold USDA Organic and Gluten-Free certifications.

SK Food Group serves a broad spectrum of foodservice customers, from independent cafes to Fortune 500 brands, supplying handcrafted sandwiches, wraps, flatbreads, burgers, protein snacks, and charcuterie boards. The company also offers private-label development and assembly, working under strict confidentiality agreements to protect client recipes and packaging intellectual property.

The firm emphasizes a hands-on, confidential partnership model, positioning itself as a collaborator that moves from concept to production while maintaining rigorous food-safety standards. Its "Your Imagination, Our Acceleration" tagline reflects a focus on rapid custom development backed by high-capacity automation.

The group's stated mission is to deliver the highest-quality cooling products through continuous R&D investment and tight control over every manufacturing step. That heritage, combined with local inventory and engineering support, is what SPAL USA presents as its differentiator in the North American market.

about:
Same Sun of Vermont was founded in 2011 in Rutland, Vermont, by Marlene and Philip Allen. The couple, a former commercial real estate appraiser and fine art dealer, had installed a rooftop array on their own home and decided to turn their experience into a family-owned business. They opened a ground-level storefront with the goal of using American-made products and creating local jobs to establish solar energy as a “new normal” in the region.

The company designs and installs custom solar arrays for residential, commercial, and institutional clients, and also provides EV charging station installation, ongoing service, maintenance, and repair. In 2018 it expanded to a 3,000-square-foot facility on West Street that features a solar awning, battery storage, and a dual EV charger. The team includes a NABCEP-certified technical sales specialist, a master electrician, and dedicated installation crews.

Same Sun serves homeowners, businesses, schools, and non-profits across Vermont, New Hampshire, and New York. Project examples include installations for VMS Construction, The Royal Group, Otter Valley Union High School, Weston Priory, and the Tunbridge Solar array in Benson and Royalton, as well as numerous residential roof and ground mounts.

The Allens started the business to empower property owners to generate their own energy and to keep young Vermonters in the state with good-paying work. The company emphasizes attention to detail, superior customer service, and sourcing premium components to ensure long-term system performance.

Sargent Metal operates from Anderson, South Carolina, where it was founded in 1975 as a family-owned metal fabrication business. The company has remained under family ownership since its inception, building a reputation for adapting to evolving industry demands.

The shop provides a full range of metal fabrication and finishing services, including CNC fiber laser cutting, CNC punching, deburring and edge rounding, CNC and robotic forming, MIG, TIG, and robotic welding, hardware insertion, powder coating, and value-added assembly. Equipment includes Trumpf laser cutting systems, and the facility handles both manual and robotic welding for materials such as aluminum, cold-rolled steel, HRPO, galvaneal, and stainless steel.

Sargent Metal serves a diverse set of industries: military (ground support systems and missile containers), people movers (elevator and escalator enclosures), power control (switchgear cabinets), safety (EMS and fire vehicle assemblies), transportation (rail and trailer components), vending (kiosks and safes), commercial vehicle (light vehicle, heavy truck, and bus parts), construction (loader, crane, and excavator components), data center (server and network infrastructure enclosures), energy management (HVAC and refrigeration housings), food equipment (oven and fryer assemblies), and HVAC (mechanical system components).

The company attributes its longevity to continuous investment in technological advancement, the ability to adapt to new markets, and an enduring commitment to its team and customers, rooted in its family-owned culture.

name: Schanz Furniture & Refinishing
old_description: Schanz Furniture & Refinishing — Handcrafted Hardwood Since 1965
about:
Schanz Furniture & Refinishing has operated in South Amana, Iowa, since 1965, when Norman and Joanna Schanz began crafting furniture in their basement. The family-owned workshop remains in the hands of the second generation, Mike and Michelle Schanz, and is situated in the historic Amana Colonies.

The shop produces custom solid-hardwood furniture — primarily cherry, oak, and walnut — along with furniture repair, refinishing, and traditional chair caning and seat weaving. Every piece is built start-to-finish by a single craftsman using traditional joinery and a proprietary formaldehyde-free conversion varnish applied in multiple hand-sanded coats. Repairs and refinishing are performed only in the shop; small gift items such as cutting boards and cheese slicers ship nationwide, while furniture is available for pickup or scheduled delivery.

Customers include homeowners commissioning one-of-a-kind dining suites or restoring heirloom pieces, tourists visiting the Amana Colonies, and gift buyers ordering small goods online. The business also serves clients seeking traditional seat-weaving patterns such as hole caning, pressed cane, rush, and splint.

The company emphasizes that its furniture is built to outlast trends and mass-produced alternatives, citing a commitment to transparency — visitors can watch the craft process — and a refusal to use particle board, MDF, or painted finishes.

Its product lineup includes hydraulic stuffers, smokehouses, grinders, slicers, band saws, vacuum sealers, tumblers, mixers, injectors, patty molders, batter and breading systems, and a full range of supplies such as casings, seasonings, packaging materials, and cutting tools. A parts department sources components from major brands, and a service team offers scheduled maintenance and emergency after‑hours calls. The operation runs from a facility that houses a test kitchen and demonstration lab, serving customers within a 150‑mile radius of St. Louis across Missouri and Illinois.

The customer base spans commercial meat processors, sausage makers, and food manufacturers producing items such as salami, summer sausage, capicola, mortadella, bologna, and pork rolls. The firm highlights its family‑owned continuity, over 80 years of industry experience, a full test kitchen for product trials, and a commitment to supplying the newest equipment at competitive prices. Emergency service availability on weekends and after hours is also promoted as a key differentiator.

about:
Scott Jordan Furniture Inc. was founded in 1980 by Scott Jordan as a furniture repair shop on Atlantic Avenue in Brooklyn's Boerum Hill neighborhood. The business began with recaning and reweaving chair seats, furniture repair, and restoration before expanding into custom solid-wood furniture production.

Today the company operates a factory workshop and showroom in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, where it designs and builds heirloom-quality sofa beds, bed frames, mattresses, and cabinetry using a hybrid of CAD/CAM-driven CNC cutting, 3D modeling, and traditional hand-finishing joinery techniques. The in-house team handles custom modifications, delivery, and installation throughout New York City, navigating tight urban spaces such as Manhattan apartments and Brooklyn brownstones.

The firm serves residential clients across the New York metro area and collaborates with upholstery partner American Leather on complex pieces. Its showroom displays over 25 floor models and full fabric libraries, allowing customers to experience materials and finishes firsthand.

Founder Scott Jordan emphasizes non-toxic, sustainable materials—sourcing Pennsylvania cherry, Ohio/Indiana walnut, Appalachian oak, and Eastern Linden from managed forests—and applies hand-rubbed natural oil and wax finishes. The company's manufacturing paradigm shifted to full CAD/CAM in 1999, enabling one-at-a-time production with high customization for NYC interiors.

about:
Sea Fresh USA, Inc. was founded in 1981 in North Kingstown, Rhode Island. The company began as a shoreside partner for seafood brands and has since grown into a vertically integrated processor of wild-caught squid and finfish. In 2023, it joined the American Seafood Partners family of brands, expanding its access to vessels, docks, and raw materials.

The company manages the full supply chain from fishing through packing at its BRC-certified facility in North Kingstown. Its dedicated fleet unloads at the Port of Galilee in Narragansett, providing access to a significant portion of Northeast seafood landings. The plant operates year-round, cleaning squid by hand to customer specifications using both blast and contact freezers. Flagship items include Boston Loligo (Doryteuthis pealeii) and Boston Illex (Illex illecebrosus), alongside imported squid species and local finfish.

Sea Fresh serves major house brands, global foodservice distributors, and restaurant chains through private-label and co-packing partnerships. Its private-label expertise spans decades, with the facility packing custom-branded cases for white-label customers across retail and foodservice channels.

The company differentiates itself through vertical integration, MSC-certified sustainable squid, and strict BRC food safety compliance. It emphasizes traceable chain-of-custody and brand protection, positioning its locally caught, locally processed calamari as a premium product for chefs and culinary professionals.

about:
Serán Bioscience, LLC is a contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) headquartered in Bend, Oregon. Founded in 2016 by Dan Smithey, Ph.D., who serves as president and CEO, the company began as an integrated provider of drug product development, formulation, and manufacturing solutions for pharmaceutical and biotechnology clients.

The company offers a full continuum of services from preformulation and formulation development through dosage form development and cGMP manufacturing. Its capabilities span oral solid dosage forms — including capsules, tablets, powder-in-bottle, multiparticulates, and mini-tablets — as well as enabling technologies such as spray drying, hot melt extrusion, fluid bed coating, film coating, and particle size reduction via jet and nano milling. Serán operates modern development facilities and is constructing a 100,000-square-foot commercial manufacturing campus to support late-stage clinical and commercial-scale production. The team has grown to over 200 scientists, engineers, and operations staff.

Serán serves pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies advancing molecules from discovery through commercialization. Its clients rely on the firm for material-sparing prototype screening, technology selection for enabled formulations (spray drying, lipid-based systems, particle engineering), and scalable clinical manufacturing of solid oral and inhalable particulates.

The company differentiates itself through its proprietary "Right From the Start™" development paradigm, which integrates drug product intermediate and drug product development in parallel to accelerate timelines. Leadership emphasizes flexibility in unit operations, adaptable manufacturing suites, and on-site ICH stability storage as key to meeting client milestones.

ShackletonThomas operates from Bridgewater, Vermont, where it was founded in 1987 by Charles Shackleton and Miranda Thomas. The two artisans established a workshop dedicated to handcrafted furniture and pottery, rooting their practice in the New England tradition of making objects by hand.

The operation includes a retail space and studio viewing platform open to visitors several days a week. While headcount and annual volume are not disclosed, the workshop handles both standard collections and custom commissions, such as a cocktail cabinet and a drop‑leaf table documented in the company’s journal.

ShackletonThomas sells directly to consumers through its website and the Bridgewater Mill store, serving the residential furnishings and gift markets. Custom pieces have been created for private clients and hospitality settings, as illustrated by the cocktail cabinet project. The company also engages a community of followers through a newsletter and seasonal open‑house events.

The founders describe their mission as “art for living—creating unique, extraordinary pieces that have soul and life,” emphasizing that every object is made to be treasured for generations. This philosophy of handcrafted longevity distinguishes the brand in a market dominated by mass production.

Sheet Metal Werks, Inc. operates from Arlington Heights, Illinois, in the Chicago metropolitan area. The company was founded in 1987 by Kevin Ryan and his father, who began fabricating sheet metal in a Des Plaines shop while Kevin and his wife Sue managed operations from their kitchen table. Its customer base consists largely of mechanical and HVAC contractors such as Amco Inc., CT Mechanical, Energy Matters, Hartwig Mechanical, and Sun Mechanical Systems. The company also provides preconstruction estimating from bid-set or BIM-coordinated drawings.

The business was built on a “never say no to work” philosophy inherited from Kevin’s father, and it maintains a union workforce. Management emphasizes on-time delivery from indoor loading docks, nationwide shipping at competitive rates, and a one-stop-shop approach that includes a full line of HVAC accessories.

about:
Sico East Coast, Inc. operates from Sanford, Florida, as the U.S. East Coast arm of the SICO Global Group. The entity was formed in 2016 when Austria-based SICO Technology GmbH acquired the former SGI USA and rebranded it as Sico East Coast Inc. The parent company, founded in 1981 in Bad Bleiberg, Austria, began as a specialist in quartz and silicon processing for the semiconductor industry.

The company manufactures high-purity custom components — quartz, silicon, and technical ceramics — for semiconductor, fiber-optic, and optical applications. Its capabilities span machining of technical ceramics, quartz fabrication, silicon carrier and injector production, and a refurbishing program that includes repair and cleaning of used parts. The global group employs nearly 150 people across five locations in Austria, Singapore, and the United States, with complete fabrication abilities at each site.

Primary customers are semiconductor original equipment manufacturers and fabs that run batch and single-wafer furnaces. Sico supplies furnace parts for various OEM furnace brands and has developed a patented silicon injector that can remain in service for up to three months without particle deposition, reducing downtime and boosting chip yields. The firm also serves the fiber-optic and optical sectors with precision quartz and ceramic components.

Sico differentiates itself through patented manufacturing methods, notably the long-life silicon injector, and maintains ISO 9001:2015 certification across its operations. The company emphasizes sustainability via its refurbishing services, which extend product life and lower costs for customers.

about:
Signature Metal Works is based in Arlington Heights, Illinois. The company was founded in 2004 by Peter and his wife Lyuba, building on a family metalworking tradition that spans four generations and over 100 years, originating in Ukraine with Peter’s grandfather Ivan. Peter, a veteran who served in the U.S. Army, immigrated in 1999 and worked on projects including the John Hancock Tower before launching the business with his sons Alex and Ilya.

The shop operates from a 10,000-square-foot facility and handles custom metal fabrication, design, and installation in-house. Capabilities include wrought iron railings, stairs, balconies, gates, staircases, commercial installations, and furniture, with finishes such as powder coating and weather-resistant paint. The team uses both classical and modern techniques to produce one-off pieces from scratch.

Signature Metal Works serves residential and commercial clients within a 50-mile radius of Chicago. Notable projects include railings for the House of Blues and the Aragon Ballroom, entrance work for Giordano’s at Navy Pier, and a remodel for Colectivo Coffee in Wicker Park.

The company emphasizes a “one-stop shop” model, controlling quality from conception to completion, and avoids cookie-cutter solutions by tailoring each project to the client’s space and aesthetic.

about:
Silfab Solar Inc. operates its U.S. manufacturing headquarters in Burlington, Washington, with additional production facilities in Fort Mill, South Carolina, and a corporate office in Mississauga, Ontario. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or ownership structure, but it identifies as a North American solar manufacturer with three domestic factories.

Silfab designs and manufactures photovoltaic modules for residential, commercial, and utility-scale markets. Its product lines include the Elite Series (back-contact technology, up to 420 W), Prime Series (black-on-black residential panels up to 440 W), Commercial Series (high-power-density modules up to 590 W), and Utility NTC bifacial panels (up to 640 W, nearly 23% efficiency). All three North American plants run fully automated production lines with advanced robotics and hold ISO 9001:2015 certification.

The company sells through distributors and installers across the United States and Canada. Its panels have been deployed in projects such as the YWCA Bellingham historic preservation retrofit, the Suquamish Tribe's solar-plus-storage installation, Infinity Drain's commercial rooftop in Massachusetts, Fisherman's Pavilion community solar in California, Brave & Maiden Estate in Oregon, and the SWIF RACK commercial array in Grants Pass, Oregon.

Silfab emphasizes that its panels are engineered specifically for North American climate conditions, citing low defect rates and one of the industry's most comprehensive warranties—25-year product and 30-year linear performance coverage on the Utility series. The Elite Series is marketed as exclusively made in the USA, using conductive backsheet and integrated cell designs to maximize light capture.

about:
Silicon Ranch Corporation, headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, began operations in 2011 with two employees. The company pioneered utility-scale solar development in the Southeast, commissioning the first such projects in Tennessee, Georgia, Mississippi, Arkansas, and Kentucky. It remains privately held, with no public disclosure of individual founders.

The firm develops, owns, and operates utility-scale solar and battery storage projects across 15 states, with more than 4,000 megawatts in operation and over 5 gigawatts contracted. Its integrated model covers planning, construction, operations, and eventual decommissioning. In addition to power generation, Silicon Ranch runs a regenerative land management program that grazes more than 2,000 sheep and cattle on project sites, supported by a proprietary CattleTracker™ system and a 26,000-square-foot lambing barn at the Houston Solar Project.

Customers include electric utilities and cooperatives such as BrightRidge and Georgia Power, commercial and industrial partners like Volkswagen and Aerojet Rocketdyne, and landowners who lease acreage for solar farms. The company also serves corporate buyers through Clearloop, a subsidiary that sells carbon reclamation tied to new solar construction.

Silicon Ranch differentiates itself by retaining long-term ownership of every project, a record of delivering every power purchase agreement since inception, and a focus on restoring soil health and biodiversity through agrivoltaics. Partnerships with SOLARCYCLE for module recycling and with First Solar and Nextracker for domestic equipment sourcing further underscore its supply-chain commitments.

The firm emphasizes continuous quality improvement, cost control, and on‑time delivery as the foundation of its customer satisfaction philosophy. Its hiring strategy focuses on retaining skilled personnel to maintain technical expertise and regional economic contribution.

about:
SisTech Manufacturing operates from a purpose-built facility in Bend, Oregon. The company was founded by industry veterans with deep experience in electronics manufacturing, though a specific founding year is not disclosed. The leadership team includes CEO Brad Kennedy, formerly VP of Operations at Vadatech Inc. and General Manager at GE Fanuc Embedded Systems Group; Operations lead Tyler Eggleston, with background at Raytheon and Collins Aerospace; and Supply Chain manager Mike Greer, a 30-year veteran of Arrow Electronics.

SisTech provides contract electronic manufacturing and mechanical assembly services, specializing in turnkey and kitted printed circuit board assemblies from quick-turn prototypes to high-volume production. Its capabilities include surface-mount placement down to 01005 components, BGA/microBGA/LGA/CSP/PoP assembly, selective soldering, in-house conformal coating, and a full suite of testing — automated optical inspection (2D/3D), X-ray with CT scan, functional and in-circuit test. The Bend facility houses six Europlacer SMT lines, Mirtec AOI, Nordson DAGE X-ray, ERSA and Aqueous Tech equipment. The company also offers design-for-manufacturing feedback, PCB layout support, obsolescence management, box-build integration, and a counterfeit-parts prevention program.

The company serves high-technology customers in defense, aerospace, energy, embedded electronics, and consumer electronics across the Pacific Northwest and nationally. It targets partners with mid- to high-range production volumes, defined production roadmaps, and requirements for rigorous quality, documentation, and traceability — explicitly avoiding one-off prototypes with no production intent and ultra-high-volume commodity builds.

SisTech differentiates itself through a lifetime manufacturing warranty, proactive DFM engagement, and a partnership model that includes early component procurement against customer forecasts. Its quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2015, ITAR registered, and CMMC Level 1, with staff certified to IPC-A-610 and IPC-7711/7721. The leadership team’s collective 130-plus years of experience underpins a focus on complex, high-reliability assemblies and long-term supply-chain stability.

name: Sky's Offroad Design & Sky Manufacturing
old_description: These springs boast a 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place finish in The Ultra4 4600 Class against 4-links and V8 power.  We have continually tweaked these to perfection through rigorous miles of trail and desert racing since 2004!
about:
Sky's Offroad Design & Sky Manufacturing operates from Springfield, Oregon. The company traces its roots to 2004, when founder Sky began developing and racing suspension components in the Ultra4 4600 Class, earning first, second, and third-place finishes against four-link and V8-powered competitors. That competition history continues to drive product development today.

The business designs and manufactures off-road suspension and steering systems for Ford F-Series and Bronco (1980–1997), Toyota, Chevrolet, Suzuki, and Dodge platforms. Core processes include CNC machining of 6061-T6 aluminum rotor hats and other components, welding of weld-in bungs and brackets, and assembly of kits that combine Timken unit bearings, alloy hardware, and custom-fabricated brackets. The product line spans leaf-spring kits, coil-over conversion kits, four-link kits, crossover steering conversions, brake kits, motor mounts, and a range of small hardware items.

Customers are primarily off-road enthusiasts and racers building or upgrading vehicles for trail, desert, and competitive use.

about:
Slate Hill Cattle Company operates from Portsmouth, Rhode Island, on Aquidneck Island. The company raises Pinzgauer cattle on a grass-fed, rotational-grazing system that emphasizes soil health and biodiversity. Beyond premium beef, the ranch practices zero-waste utilization: suet is rendered into tallow for cooking, skincare, and candle making, while organs are freeze-dried into custom dog treats. The herd is managed with a blend of traditional husbandry and modern technology to monitor herd health and resource efficiency.

Products are marketed directly to consumers seeking ethically raised beef and natural pet treats, with an emphasis on local and regional customers who value transparent, sustainable sourcing.

Welch frames the venture as a family affair dedicated to preserving the Pinzgauer breed and ranching heritage for future generations. The operation’s stated goals include reducing its carbon footprint, expanding educational outreach on sustainable farming, and advancing regenerative practices to serve as long-term stewards of the land.

about:
SolarPod is based in Shakopee, Minnesota. Founded in 2009 by Mouli Vaidyanathan, who holds a PhD in Metallurgical Engineering and is a licensed Professional Engineer and Master Electrician, the company began as Mouli Engineering, selling modular ground-mounted DIY solar systems and installing conventional solar arrays. Vaidyanathan recognized that traditional racking methods damaged roofs with numerous penetrations, prompting him to develop a non-penetrating racking solution.

The company manufactures two patented racking systems—Z-Rack for sloped roofs and Z-Lite for flat roofs—in its Shakopee facility. Both systems are designed to eliminate roof holes, using a weighted, non-penetrating design that has been wind-tested and approved in over 300 jurisdictions. SolarPod also provides full installation services for residential, commercial, and utility-scale projects, and offers modular DIY kits that can be configured for grid-tied, off-grid, or hybrid operation. To date, the company reports 16 MW of installed capacity across more than 1,000 installations.

SolarPod serves homeowners, businesses, and solar developers across Minnesota and beyond. Its racking products are sold to installers, contractors, and developers for projects ranging from small residential arrays to a 408 kW commercial installation at Edina’s Cornelia Elementary School. The company also markets directly to DIY customers through its online store, where systems are priced by panel count and configuration.

Vaidyanathan founded SolarPod to address the structural damage and water-leak risks inherent in conventional racking. A partnership with OneTreePlanted adds a tree-planting component to every product sold.

The company serves semiconductor manufacturers, MEMS producers (pressure sensors, microphones, gyroscopes, accelerometers), and industrial sectors including consumer electronics, automotive, and medical devices. Its microscopes are deployed from development labs to high-volume production floors worldwide.

Sonix emphasizes its global support infrastructure and long-standing innovation leadership as key differentiators. Sound Manufacturing, Inc. was founded in 1984 in Old Saybrook, Connecticut, by Brian Cote and Kenneth Oliver. Designs follow IEEE standards, and the firm emphasizes tailored solutions for specific customer requirements.

SEECO serves the electrical utility sector, supplying equipment for transmission and substation projects. Its switches and complementary devices are used in sectionalizing and switching applications across utility networks.

The company cites its engineer-driven culture and ISO 9001:2015 certification as foundations for reliability and performance. Notable innovations include unitized transmission switches, line-post sensors for automation, vacuum interrupters, and the Smart Universal Motor Operator (SUMO), a universal motor with torsional or reciprocating capabilities. Its mission emphasizes intelligently engineered solutions for greater performance, reliability, and ease of installation, backed by exceptional service and support.

The company maintains a 200,000-square-foot inventory of new surplus and reconditioned industrial electrical equipment, including circuit breakers, starters, contactors, renewal parts, bus plugs, disconnects, PLCs, motor control centers, and transformers. It also provides repair services for molded case breakers, air breakers, motor starters, and PLC automation equipment, backed by a 12-month warranty. Custom engineering, retrofits, and upgrades are offered alongside field service and preventative maintenance.

Southland serves industrial customers requiring electrical equipment, repairs, and custom solutions. Its client base spans facilities that rely on low- and medium-voltage power distribution and control systems, with 24/7 emergency support and courier service available.

The company emphasizes fast turnaround—average order time for molded case breakers is one to two days, and most projects are completed in one to two weeks—along with same-day and next-day shipping options. A family-business culture and certified technician staff underpin its service model.

name: Southrock Engineering Inc.
old_description: Reverse Engineering for Printed Circuit Boards Assembly (PCBA)
about:
Southrock Engineering Inc. is based in Mesa, Arizona, and was founded in 2006 by Peter and Christine Hall. Both had worked in the electronics industry for over 20 years, and in 2006 they acquired JR Electronics from the estate of its original founder, a company that had produced specialized cable assemblies for industrial customers for more than a decade. With backgrounds in electronic hardware design, microprocessors, and software, the Halls expanded from contract design projects into full electronic manufacturing, investing in modern wire processing, crimping equipment, and surface-mount pick-and-place capability.

The company designs and assembles custom printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) using both surface-mount and through-hole processes, builds custom cable and wire harness assemblies, provides full-service box build assembly with enclosure integration, and offers PCB and cable assembly prototyping from single units to small batches. It also performs PCBA reverse engineering to address obsolete designs, hard-to-source components, or offshore vendor constraints. All assembly work is performed to IPC standards; the shop is UL certified and RoHS compliant. There are no minimum order quantities, and the facility supports volumes from prototype through production runs.

Southrock serves a range of sectors including aerospace and defense, commercial, industrial, marine, telecommunications, automotive, energy, lighting, health, safety, and utility markets. Customers include manufacturers of automation and control systems, monitoring systems, LED and lighting solutions, electronics and power solutions, and specialized automation equipment.

The business was started to provide a complete range of electronic design and assembly under one roof, and its reverse engineering service was developed specifically to help clients re-engineer PCBA and wire harness products to avoid tariffs and overcome supply-chain hurdles with offshore vendors. The company emphasizes local engineering support, quick turnaround, and freight savings from its Mesa facility.

Southwest Decoratives & Kokopelli Quilting Company operates from Bernalillo, New Mexico, where it has been based since relocating from Albuquerque. The business was founded in 1992 by Mary-Jo McCarthy as a home-based venture selling Southwestern-themed quilt patterns through a small black-and-white catalog. It remains family-owned, with McCarthy and her family running the operation.

The company retails a curated selection of Southwestern-style fabrics, quilt patterns, kits, and notions for quilting, sewing, cross stitch, and general crafting. After launching an e-commerce site in 1994, it opened a 2,500-square-foot brick-and-mortar shop in 2001. The store moved to its current location on US Highway 550 in Bernalillo, where it also serves wholesale buyers. Inventory includes cotton prints, block-of-the-month programs, clothing patterns, and craft supplies.

Customers include individual quilters, sewists, and crafters across the United States, Canada, and Europe, as well as other retail shops purchasing wholesale. The shop attracted national recognition in 2013 when Better Homes & Gardens Quilt Sampler Magazine named it a Top 10 quilt shop.

The founding mission was to share the enchantment of Southwest culture with the sewing and crafting community. The company emphasizes access to distinctive regional designs and competitive pricing on quality fabrics, patterns, and kits.

Its product lines include Reverse Bayonet, MIL-DTL-38999, 95234, 5015, 22992, 26482, and 85049 series, along with accessories such as dust caps, dummy receptacles, crimp contact wire adapters, termination bands, and flange gaskets. Spacecraft serves the railway and transit, military, aerospace, and general industrial sectors, supplying connectors that meet stringent environmental and performance requirements. Its customer base includes prime contractors and maintenance organizations that need reliable circular interconnects for demanding applications.

Spacecraft differentiates itself through its AS9100-qualified quality system and a consultative approach that leverages in-house engineering and technical sales expertise to deliver tailored connector solutions for harsh environments.

Spartan Home Pros was founded in 2020 and is headquartered in Hazlet, New Jersey, with additional offices in Bridgewater and Chatham. The company operates as a licensed and insured electrical and HVAC service provider under New Jersey Electrical Contractor Business Permit #34EB01810700, serving residential and commercial customers across Central New Jersey.

The firm provides a full range of electrical services including panel upgrades (100‑amp to 200‑amp), EV charger installation for brands such as Tesla, ChargePoint, and Ford, emergency repair, new circuit wiring, lighting and ceiling‑fan installation, whole‑home generator systems (as an authorized Generac installer), surge protection, and electrical inspections. Commercial work covers tenant fit‑outs, three‑phase distribution, lighting retrofits, and code corrections, while a dedicated older‑home division handles fuse‑box replacement, knob‑and‑tube rewiring, and Federal Pacific/Zinsco panel swaps. All work is performed by the company’s own crews; no subcontractors are used.

Customers include homeowners, retail storefronts, restaurants, cafes, salons, dental and medical practices, professional offices, and industrial facilities such as warehouses and production plants requiring high‑bay lighting. The company’s certified installer status for Tesla, ChargePoint, Emporia, and Lutron controls, together with its Generac authorization, allows it to support EV‑charging infrastructure and backup‑power projects across the region.

Spartan Home Pros differentiates itself with flat, upfront pricing that eliminates hourly meters, a permit‑handling service that files with local townships, and 24/7 emergency response answered around the clock. The two physical office locations in Hazlet and Bridgewater ensure local coverage rather than a broad service radius drawn from a distant base.

Specfab serves customers in pharmaceutical, chemical, and food processing and packaging facilities worldwide, as well as broader industrial and commercial sectors. The company handles projects ranging from single custom fabrications to high-volume production runs.

The company’s stated mission is to deliver a quality product solution at a fair price, emphasizing service and delivery as constant priorities. Its ISO 9001:2015 certification and in-house CMM inspection with PPAP first-article validation underscore a focus on documented quality control.

old_description: Founded in 1990 with the idea that the company can succeed by making short runs of wire cords.
about:
Specialty Wire & Cord Sets operates from Hamden, Connecticut, where it was founded in 1990 by Lee and Lynn Campo. The company began with the premise that a business could thrive by focusing on short-run production of wire cords, a niche that larger manufacturers often overlook. Today, the Campo family continues to own and manage the operation, which runs on 100% solar power.

The shop produces custom coiled cords, retractable wires, and curly cables for power and communication applications. Its manufacturing lines handle thermoset rubber (SVO, SJOOW, SOOW), PVC (SJT, SJTOW, SVT), TPE (SVEO, SJEOW, SEOW), and TPU jacketing, with options for shielded and non-shielded configurations in both standard and miniature sizes. The facility stocks a range of standard cords for same-day shipment, while custom orders can be as short as one inch or extend up to 20 feet with a maximum 100-foot extension. All wire is UL-listed or CSA-certified and RoHS compliant.

Customers span transportation, medical and dental equipment, aircraft ground support, robotics, hand-held remote controls, retail displays, overhead doors, gaming equipment, machine tools, and security devices. The company serves wholesale buyers and OEMs that need low-volume or prototype runs as well as larger production quantities.

The founders' original insight—that small orders deserve the same attention as large ones—remains the guiding principle. Management emphasizes personalized service, with quotes returned within one business day and direct access to senior staff. The solar-powered facility underscores a commitment to sustainable manufacturing.

Spectral Products is headquartered in Putnam, Connecticut, with additional offices in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Seoul, South Korea. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed. It operates as a manufacturer of optical instrumentation.

The company designs and builds spectrometers, monochromators, light sources, integrating spheres, detectors, fiber-optic accessories, adapters, and filter wheels. An Optics Division also supplies optical coatings and coated optics for high-energy applications.

Spectral Products serves industrial, laboratory, research, and scientific markets, working directly with system designers and end users. The company maintains international representatives in Europe, Asia, and Australia.

The firm attributes its differentiation to an innovative direct-drive technique introduced more than a decade ago, which it says revolutionized computer-based spectrometers and monochromators by delivering high performance at lower cost. Its SM miniature spectrometers are marketed as combining essential features and optimal performance in a small footprint.

Stack serves original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), original design manufacturers (ODMs), contract manufacturers (CMs), and Tier 1 suppliers across industries that require high-reliability electronic components, including aerospace and defense applications implied by its AS9120B certification.

The company emphasizes a solutions-oriented approach, citing on-time delivery of critical items, strategic cost savings, strict supplier vetting, and continuous improvement tracked through supplier performance metrics as key differentiators.

about:
Staco Systems was founded in 1958 in Costa Mesa, California, originally operating as Staco Switch. The company began by supplying lighted pushbutton display switches to the aviation and defense firms clustered in Southern California, with its first Series 30 switch flying on a Fokker F-27 in 1960. Today the headquarters is in Irvine, California, and the firm maintains sales representatives in more than 35 countries.

The product line has expanded from those early switches to include rugged keyboards and keypads, electronic controllers, panel assemblies, edge‑lit panels, and complete cockpit control assemblies. Staco emphasizes custom engineering, citing advances in optics, weight reduction, and miniaturization as core technical capabilities. The company serves as a manufacturer of human‑machine interface components, producing both standard and custom solutions for demanding applications.

Staco’s customer base spans military, aerospace, shipboard, ground vehicle, naval, industrial, power‑generation, and flight‑simulation markets. The company references its long‑standing relationships with major aerospace and defense primes, though specific client names are not disclosed. Historical examples include the Fokker F‑27 installation and ongoing supply to military and commercial aviation programs.

Staco attributes its longevity to a commitment to quality and custom problem‑solving, backed by certifications such as AS9100 and MIL‑SPEC. The firm states that its differentiation lies in superior engineering and continual technology development that enable unique custom solutions tailored to customer specifications.

name: Stark Mountain Woodworking Co
old_description: Blending time honored wood craft with the tech of today in the mountains of Vermont since 1993
about:
Stark Mountain Woodworking Co. was founded in 1993 in New Haven, Vermont, a town of about 1,800 people in the state's mountainous region. The business began as a two-person shop and has grown to a team of more than 20 craftspeople operating from a 24,000-square-foot facility.

The company provides full-service custom woodworking, producing cabinetry for homes and offices, furniture, and architectural millwork for institutions such as museums, libraries, and colleges. Each project moves through design collaboration, 2D and 3D shop drawings created with AutoCAD, DataCAD, AlphaCam, and Cabinet Vision, CNC fabrication on three- and five-axis routers, moulding, sanding, edge banding, finishing in a dedicated spray booth, and final assembly and installation. A bandsaw mill and vacuum kiln give the shop control over lumber from tree to finished product, and a full metal shop handles architectural finishes in stainless steel and bronze.

Clients include architects, interior designers, general contractors, and homeowners. Notable project types range from residential and commercial interiors to institutional work for colleges, libraries, and museums.

Stark Mountain has been FSC-certified since 2001 and sources a large percentage of its lumber within a 30-mile radius. The facility runs on roughly 60 percent solar power, with a 54 kW hillside array and a 34 kW rooftop array, and is heated by a pelletizer that converts shop sawdust into fuel. A bike-to-work program has logged over 145,000 commuter miles since 2006.

name: Steadfast Farms
old_description: The New Standard in USDA-inspected Poultry Processing in New England
about:
Steadfast Farms is based in Bethlehem, Connecticut. Founded in 2017 by Jared McCool, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran who began farming after his honorable discharge in 2014, the veteran-owned operation started as a continuation of military service, applying principles of discipline and resilience to agriculture.

The company runs Connecticut’s only USDA-inspected poultry slaughter and processing facility, providing fee-for-service processing to more than 180 farms across the Northeast. The plant is certified for USDA Organic slaughter and holds Animal Welfare Approved verification, enabling interstate sales of processed birds. In addition to contract processing, Steadfast Farms raises its own pasture-raised poultry—quail, chicken, turkey, pheasant, and chukar partridge—using regenerative farming practices. The facility also offers parting, grinding, sausage making, and stock production.

Steadfast Farms serves two primary customer groups: independent poultry farmers who need USDA-inspected processing to bring birds to market, and wholesale buyers such as restaurants, retailers, and food-service distributors. The company also works with game-bird clubs and other B2B farm partners throughout the region.

McCool has stated that the business was founded to extend his service to the domestic community, emphasizing regenerative land stewardship, humane animal handling, and transparent production. The company’s stated values—Rooted in Resilience, Integrity in Every Bite, Delivering the Promise, Pioneer Partner Empower—reflect a commitment to consistent quality and ethical farming from hatch to harvest.
